The graph of the second derivative $y={f}^{″}(x)$ of the function $f(x)$ is shown above. 
Find the intervals on which the function $f(x)$ is concave up.

The graph above shows $y={f}^{″}(x),$ where the function $f(x)$ is defined on $[-5,5].$ Find the intervals on which the function $f(x)$ is concave up.
feedback.worked_solution:
A function $f(x)$ is concave up over an interval $(a,b)$ if ${f}^{″}(x)>0$ for all $x\in (a,b).$

On the given graph of $y={f}^{″}(x)$, we can see that ${f}^{″}(x)>0$ on the intervals $(-5,-1)$ and  $(1,5).$  Therefore, the function $f(x)$ is concave up on the intervals $(-5,-1)$ and  $(1,5).$
